findings.text: the evidence anchor reports the gate wall clock as 10.09 s while citing xpoint-cell/render-gate.log, whose own summary line reads '4 passed, 1 skipped in 11.40s'; the plan landing comment repeats the same 10.09 s. The named artifact contradicts the figure quoted from it. It is a wall clock rather than a correctness claim and the manifest's after_suite field carries the log's 11.40 s, so the discrepancy is confined to the two prose records.

xpoint-cell/render-defect-reproduction.log has no revision/tree/command header, unlike render-gate.log and render-negative-control.log, so its claim to be the base revision 1cfd3fd4c2e2 re-run is not checkable from the log itself. I corroborated it from the code instead (the printed inventory matches 1cfd3fd4c's marker literals exactly and shows no hollow glyph, which the repaired painter cannot produce for the analytic set), so the reproduction is real -- but a later reader cannot establish the revision without repeating that inspection.

the live-spin half of the check exercises the vocabulary only for the axis marker on the single reference panel; the hollow analytic classification and the saddle literals are asserted against the committed render receipt, and nothing in the check ties the receipt's source_revision to the tree the gate runs on, so a receipt regenerated at a different revision would still pass. The worker discloses the receipt-vs-live split in its manifest; the missing source_revision assertion is the concrete tightening available.

justifications.durability: the deliverable is committed at e31426d26c4df08015ae5c5980aa1decc38fb678 in the assigned worktree with a substantive body and no AI trailer; the five SVG panels and their PNG companions are committed (git add -f, since the figure trees are gitignored) with the receipt and all four logs beside them, and the landing record and evidence anchor are in the same commit. The worktree is clean after my runs. Durability loses a little because the defect-reproduction log carries no revision/tree/command header, unlike its gate and control siblings, so its base-revision claim is not self-evidencing from the log alone.
justifications.evidence: I reproduced the node's own gate rather than reading its claim: `python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -s --no-header -q tests/test_xpoint_cell_wedge_render.py` exits 0 with 4 passed, 1 skipped (log review-gate.log in my run dir), and with NOVA_XPOINT_WEDGE_MUTATION=inverted-axis-marker it exits 1 with the marker check red and the offending glyph named: "the vocabulary check admitted a marker outside the draw_nulls vocabulary: ['v']" (review-negative-control.log). I confirmed the guard is not vacuous -- it reads the classised artist (marker literal plus whether markerfacecolor is 'none'), which is what makes an inverted triangle a recorded violation. I corroborated the defect reproduction independently rather than trusting the log: the committed inventory (marker='^' face='#2563eb', marker='v' face='#d97706') is exactly what the base painter emits (axis_marker="^" in the analytic colour, axis_marker="v" in the read colour at 1cfd3fd4c, no hollow glyph), and I verified nova/media/poloidal.py's other_x_points branch is the only route that draws hollow. The one evidence defect is a misquoted figure (finding below).
justifications.fit: no plan, phase, sprint or followup identifier appears in any source symbol, filename or comment: the new symbols are mechanism-named (SOLVED_AXIS_MARKER, NULL_GLYPH_VOCABULARY, _marker_glyphs, _draw_panel, render_only), and the commit subject/bodies describe the drawing change rather than the plan item. The evidence anchor cites by anchor id only, and I read only the cited section of the 780 KB record as the fence instructed. The repair sits in the painter lane the plan assigns it to and touches only the declared paths.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the stated goal -- repair the five xpoint-cell/single-null-wedges panels so the coincident analytic and solved null sets are drawn in the draw_nulls vocabulary without the ochre-over-blue hourglass and with a legend naming each set -- is delivered and independently reproduced. I read the committed SVGs/PNGs (110 and 500): both now draw an up triangle for the axis and a cross for the saddle, the solved set solid ochre and the analytic reference hollow blue, with a four-entry legend naming solved/analytic and axis/saddle, no axis furniture, and the vessel wall closed around the section. The receipt (schema nova.xpoint-cell-wedge-render) records every panel's glyph count per set, both title lines, the four legend labels and wall_node_count 121, and I re-ran the gate and the declared control myself: green unmutated, red under the mutation.
justifications.scope_discipline: the commit touches exactly the declared write paths (benchmarks/xpoint_cell_wedge_oracle.py, tests/test_xpoint_cell_wedge_render.py, the xpoint-cell figure directory, the plan and the evidence archive) and nothing outside them; git status in the worktree is clean. The plan edit is a landing comment only -- it does not resolve the driving followup f-cca-repair-minor-rendering-defects or close the node, which the worker's own contract forbids it to do. No other node's paths were touched.
